note: One narrow idea per Short. Hooks and examples are our own words, never quotes.

chapters.title: Night 1: Your past does not decide your future

episodes.title: Your goal, not your past
episodes.hook: Your past isn't holding you back. Your goal is.
episodes.angle: Behaviour serves a goal you have right now, not a cause from long ago. Example: someone who 'can't' go to parties because of an old embarrassment, while the real goal today is to stay safe from new judgment.

episodes.title: Anger is a tool
episodes.hook: You didn't lose your temper. You used it.
episodes.angle: Anger is produced on demand to get your way. Example: snapping at a waiter, then answering a phone call from a friend in a sweet voice one second later.

episodes.title: What shyness does for you
episodes.hook: You're not shy. Shyness is doing a job for you.
episodes.angle: A trait you say you hate can protect you: if you never speak up, nobody can reject the real you. Example: the quiet new colleague at lunch.

episodes.title: The 'if only' life
episodes.hook: The most comfortable sentence in the world starts with 'if only'.
episodes.angle: Keeping a dream untested keeps it safe. Example: the novelist who never sends in the manuscript, so the answer can never be no.

episodes.title: You can pick again
episodes.hook: You picked your personality when you were ten. You can pick again.
episodes.angle: The way you see the world and yourself was a choice made early, and it can be made again today. Example: 'I'm just a pessimist' as a habit, not a fact.

episodes.title: Comfortable unhappiness
episodes.hook: You're not stuck. You're comfortable.
episodes.angle: Known unhappiness feels safer than unknown change, so we choose not to change. Example: the old car that rattles but you know every sound of it.

episodes.title: Use what you have
episodes.hook: Stop asking what you were given.
episodes.angle: What matters is how you use what you have, not what you got. Example: two game characters with the same weak starting stats, one keeps complaining at the start screen, one plays.

episodes.title: Same past, different meaning
episodes.hook: Two people. Same bad childhood. Opposite lives.
episodes.angle: Events do not decide us, the meaning we give them does. Example: two siblings from the same loud house, one says 'so I can't trust anyone', the other 'so I will build a calm home'.

chapters.title: Night 2: Every problem is about other people

episodes.title: Alone in the universe
episodes.hook: If you were the only person in the universe, your problems would disappear.
episodes.angle: Every worry needs other people in it: even loneliness needs others to exist. Example: would you care about your height on an empty planet?

episodes.title: A number you compared
episodes.hook: Your biggest flaw is a number you compared to someone else's.
episodes.angle: Feeling inferior is a personal reading, not a fact. Example: being 'short' only hurts next to someone; it can also mean people relax around you.

episodes.title: Feeling versus excuse
episodes.hook: 'I'm not smart enough' isn't a feeling. It's an excuse.
episodes.angle: Feeling behind can push you forward; it turns harmful when it becomes 'because of A, I can't do B'. Example: 'no degree, so no point applying'.

episodes.title: Why people brag
episodes.hook: People who brag are telling you how small they feel.
episodes.angle: Showing off borrowed power (name dropping, brands, old wins) is the other side of feeling inferior. Example: the guy who mentions his famous boss in every sentence.

episodes.title: Pain as a crown
episodes.hook: Some people use their pain as a crown.
episodes.angle: Misfortune can be used to feel special and to control others. Example: the friend who rejects every bit of comfort with 'you could never understand'.

episodes.title: There is no race
episodes.hook: You're not behind. There is no race.
episodes.angle: Life is not a track where everyone runs the same way. Walk forward on a flat field and compare only with who you were yesterday. Example: scrolling through job titles of old classmates.

episodes.title: Happy for your friend
episodes.hook: Why can't you be happy for your friend?
episodes.angle: When life is a competition, every win of someone else is your loss and people become enemies. Drop the contest and they become comrades. Example: a friend's promotion message.

episodes.title: Winning the argument
episodes.hook: The moment you want to win an argument, you've already lost.
episodes.angle: When being right turns into beating the other person, it is a power struggle. Step off the stage instead. Example: a comment thread at 2 a.m.

episodes.title: I was wrong
episodes.hook: Saying 'I was wrong' is not losing.
episodes.angle: Admitting a mistake, saying sorry and stepping back are not defeat, they only feel like it when everything is a contest. Example: a couple arguing over directions.

episodes.title: Looking for flaws
episodes.hook: You didn't leave because of his flaws. You found flaws because you wanted out.
episodes.angle: We first set the goal (ending or avoiding a relationship) and then collect reasons. Example: the way he chews was cute for two years.

chapters.title: Night 3: Let go of other people's tasks

episodes.title: Not here for expectations
episodes.hook: You're not here to meet anyone's expectations.
episodes.angle: If you live for approval, you end up living someone else's life. And others are not here to meet yours. Example: choosing a study to make a parent proud.

episodes.title: Nobody is watching
episodes.hook: If no one is watching, do you still pick up the trash?
episodes.angle: Reward and punishment teach us to do good only when seen. Example: cleaning the office kitchen and waiting for someone to notice.

episodes.title: Whose task is this?
episodes.hook: You're exhausted because you keep doing homework that isn't yours.
episodes.angle: Ask who ends up living with the result of a choice: that person owns the task. Already made as the first test Short.

episodes.title: That's your task
episodes.hook: The most loving thing a parent can say: that's your task.
episodes.angle: Helping is not taking over. You can lead a horse to water. Example: a parent hovering over homework versus saying 'I'm here when you want help'.

episodes.title: Your boss dislikes you
episodes.hook: Your boss dislikes you. That's his problem. Literally.
episodes.angle: What others think of you is their task. Yours is to do your work well. Example: a manager who is cold whatever you do.

episodes.title: The price of freedom
episodes.hook: If nobody dislikes you, you're not free.
episodes.angle: Being disliked by someone is proof you are living by your own choices. It is the cost of freedom, not a goal. Example: saying no to a weekend favour.

episodes.title: Pleasing everyone
episodes.hook: Pleasing everyone is the easiest way to live. That's the problem.
episodes.angle: Promising everyone what they want means lying to yourself and to them. Example: saying yes to three plans on the same Saturday night.

episodes.title: You hold the cards
episodes.hook: You don't need them to change first.
episodes.angle: You can change your side of a relationship without waiting. Whether they respond is their task. Example: the first message after years of silence with a father.

episodes.title: No thanks needed
episodes.hook: Don't help to be thanked.
episodes.angle: The moment you give to get something back, you are bound to the other's reaction. Example: holding a door and feeling angry at the missing 'thanks'.

chapters.title: Night 4: You are not the center of the world

episodes.title: Main character of one life
episodes.hook: You're the main character. Of one life. Not everyone's.
episodes.angle: Worrying all day about how others see you is being focused on yourself. Others are not extras in your film. Example: sure that everyone saw the stain on your shirt.

episodes.title: Build where you belong
episodes.hook: You don't find where you belong. You build it.
episodes.angle: Belonging does not come from being accepted, it comes from taking part and giving. Ask what you can give, not what you get. Example: the new member of a sports club.

episodes.title: Zoom out
episodes.hook: If your office feels like the whole world, zoom out.
episodes.angle: When one small group hurts, remember the bigger ones you are part of. A storm in a cup means nothing outside the cup. Example: school drama seen from the whole town.

episodes.title: 'Good job'
episodes.hook: 'Good job' is how you talk down to someone.
episodes.angle: Praise is a judgment from above and teaches people to work for the pat on the head. Example: would you say 'well done, good boy' to your boss?

episodes.title: Thank you
episodes.hook: Say 'thank you', not 'good job'.
episodes.angle: Thanks comes from an equal and tells someone they were useful, which gives courage. Example: a kid who sets the table.

episodes.title: Worth before doing
episodes.hook: You're valuable before you do anything.
episodes.angle: People are of worth by being here, not only by what they do. Example: how you feel about a sick friend in a hospital bed who 'does' nothing.

episodes.title: Equal, not rude
episodes.hook: Treat your boss as an equal. Not rude. Equal.
episodes.angle: Different roles, same worth. Saying no to a senior person is not disrespect. Example: disagreeing in a meeting with a calm 'I see it differently'.

episodes.title: Someone goes first
episodes.hook: Someone has to go first. It can be you.
episodes.angle: Do not wait for others to cooperate before you start. Example: the first person who starts clapping, or greets the neighbour.

chapters.title: Night 5: Live fully, here and now

episodes.title: Stop saying you're great
episodes.hook: Stop telling yourself you're great.
episodes.angle: Pumping yourself up with 'I can do anything' is lying to yourself. Accept the 60 percent you got and ask how to get closer to 100. Example: a failed exam.

episodes.title: Trust without a receipt
episodes.hook: Trust people without a receipt.
episodes.angle: Trust with conditions is a loan. Deep relationships need trust that is given first. Being let down is the other person's task. Example: lending a friend your bike.

episodes.title: Too busy
episodes.hook: Being too busy is a way of hiding.
episodes.angle: Work can be an excuse to skip the rest of life: home, friends, yourself. Example: answering mail at a kid's birthday.

episodes.title: Useful without applause
episodes.hook: You don't need thanks to be useful.
episodes.angle: Happiness is the private feeling 'I am of use to someone', and it needs no audience. Example: watering the plants in a shared hallway.

episodes.title: Normal is fine
episodes.hook: You don't have to be special.
episodes.angle: Chasing 'special' comes from not accepting your normal self. Being normal is not being incapable. Example: the pressure to have a big story on social media.

episodes.title: Two kids, one wish
episodes.hook: The kid acting out and the straight-A kid want the same thing.
episodes.angle: Both want to be special. When being specially good fails, being specially bad is the easy way. Example: one classroom, two desks.

episodes.title: No peak
episodes.hook: Life isn't a climb to a peak.
episodes.angle: If life is a climb, most of it is 'on the way'. See it as a dance instead: each moment is already complete. Example: a trip where you only think about the hotel.

episodes.title: Light up today
episodes.hook: Stop planning your life. Light up today.
episodes.angle: Put a bright spotlight on now and you cannot see the past or the future, and you do not need to. Example: studying one page today instead of dreaming about the diploma.

episodes.title: No built-in meaning
episodes.hook: Life has no meaning. That's the good news.
episodes.angle: Life has no meaning given in advance, so you get to give it one. Example: an empty save file at the start of a game.

episodes.title: Your guiding star
episodes.hook: One rule so you never feel lost.
episodes.angle: As long as you keep heading toward 'being of use to others', you can choose freely and be disliked without getting lost. Example: a sailor and one fixed star.
